questions.question_text:
The cost $\$C$ of ordering pizzas varies directly with the number of pizzas $n$.
It costs $\$76$ for $8$ pizzas.
What is the equation relating $C$ and $n$?

options.why: Used the number of pizzas $8$ as $k$ instead of calculating $k=76/8=9.5$.
Used the inverse variation form instead of the direct variation form $y=kx$.
Wrote the equation with the variables swapped.

questions.question_text:
The time $t$ (days) needed to complete a job varies inversely with the number of workers $n$.
It takes $12$ days with $5$ workers.
Find the constant of variation and write an equation for $t$ in terms of $n$.

options.why: Used the direct variation form $y=kx$ instead of the inverse variation form $y=k/x$.
Used the workers value from the point instead of the constant of variation $k$.
Divided $12/5=2.4$ instead of multiplying $12\times5=60$ to find the constant of variation.

questions.question_text:
The cost $\$P$ of buying paint varies directly with the number of litres $L$, and $P=23L$.
Find the cost of $6$ litres.

options.why: Added $L$ to $k$ instead of multiplying $k$ by $L$: $23+6=29$.
Divided $k$ by $L$ instead of multiplying, then rounded $23/6$ to the nearest cent.
Used $24$ instead of the supplied coefficient $23$, giving $24\times6=144$.

questions.question_text:
In an assumed model, the intensity $I$ of light (in lux) varies inversely with the distance $d$ (in metres) from the source, and $I=\dfrac{84}{d}$.
Find the intensity at $7$ m.

options.why: Multiplied by the distance instead of dividing the constant by the distance.
Subtracted the distance from the constant instead of dividing.
Gave the constant of variation instead of substituting the distance into the equation.

questions.question_text:
The cost $\$C$ of ordering pizzas varies directly with the number of pizzas $n$, and $C=9.5n$.
How many pizzas can be bought for $\$66.50$?

options.why: Added the coefficient to the cost instead of dividing: $66.50+9.5=76$.
Used $10$ as the divisor instead of $9.5$, giving $66.50/10=6.65$, then incorrectly rounded to the nearest half to get $6.5$.
Divided $k$ by $C$ instead of dividing $C$ by $k$, then rounded $9.5/66.50=1/7$ to two decimal places.

questions.question_text:
The cost per guest $\$C$ of hiring a venue varies inversely with the number of guests $n$ sharing the cost.
The cost per guest is $\$54$ when $8$ guests share it.
How many guests are needed for the cost per guest to be $\$18$?

options.why: Confused the number of guests with the cost per guest given in the question.
Multiplied the constant of variation by the cost instead of dividing it by the cost.
Gave the constant of variation instead of solving for the number of guests.
Used the direct variation form $y=kx$ instead of the inverse variation form $y=k/x$.
Used the workers value from the point instead of the constant of variation $k$.
Divided the coordinates to get $k=18/5=3.6$ instead of multiplying to get $k=90$.

questions.question_text:
In a hypothetical assumed model, the loudness $L$ of a sound (in decibels above background) varies inversely with the distance $d$ (in metres) from the source.
At $2.5$ m the loudness is $40$ dB.
Find the loudness at $6$ m, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Truncated $100/6$ to a whole number instead of rounding to one decimal place.
Multiplied the constant by the distance instead of dividing: $100\times6=600$.
Subtracted the distance from the constant instead of dividing: $100-6=94$.

questions.question_text:
The cost per guest $\$C$ of hiring a venue varies inversely with the number of guests $n$ sharing the cost, and $C=\dfrac{600}{n}$.
How many guests are needed for the cost per guest to be exactly $\$37.50$?

options.why: Multiplied instead of dividing to find $n$: $600\times37.50=22500$.
Reversed the division, calculating $37.50/600=0.0625$ instead of $600/37.50$.
Gave the constant of variation instead of solving for the number of guests.

questions.question_text: $d$ varies inversely with $c$. If $d=50$ when $c=124$, find $d$ when $c=155$.

options.why: Added the increase in $c$ to $d$, giving $50+(155-124)=81$, instead of keeping $cd$ constant.
Uses the constant product as the new value instead of dividing by $155$.
Uses an incorrect ratio direction for inverse proportion, calculating $50\times155/124=62.5$.

questions.solution_text: For inverse proportion, $cd$ is constant. Thus $124\times50=6200$, and when $c=155$, $d=6200/155=40$.
